message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.  
I’ll give you two ways to do it:

| Method | What you’ll run | Why it’s handy |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **`gcloud` CLI** | One‑liner command that works from your terminal | Fast, no code needed |
| **REST API** | JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine endpoint | Useful if you’re building a programmatic workflow |

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with the **Compute Engine API** enabled.  
> * You need a **service account** (or user credentials) that has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role.  
> * Your project must have a **GPU quota** for the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator in the zone you choose.  
> * If you’re using the REST API, you’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-ubuntu-disk \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Where the VM lives (pick a zone that supports GPUs). |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM – plenty for a GPU‑heavy workload. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the VM running during maintenance events. |
| `--provisioning-model=STANDARD` | Uses the standard provisioning model (good for most workloads). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for fast I/O. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a shell script at first boot (e.g., to install drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you don’t need a startup script, just drop the `--metadata-from-file` line.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a Python script), here’s the JSON payload you’d POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT` with your actual project ID.  
The `instance.json` file contains the JSON above.

---

## 3️⃣  Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project ID (`YOUR_PROJECT`) |
| ✅ | Zone that supports GPUs (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.) |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| ✅ | Service account with `compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role |
| ✅ | (Optional) Startup script to install NVIDIA drivers |

---

### Final Note

Both methods will create a VM that:

* Runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS** (the latest LTS release).  
* Has **one RTX A6000 GPU** attached.  
* Uses an **SSD boot disk** of 100 GB.  
* Is located in the `us-central1-a` zone (you can change this to any zone that supports GPUs).

Happy computing! 🚀
